Saffire V-2 (cotton jersey) used 26.2 mol % oxygen at 70.7 kPa [R028].
- The Saffire IV and V paper lists the same 70.7 kPa and 26.2 % [R066].
The two-sided PMMA sample in Saffire VI-3 burned for 780 s [R030].
The LUCI capsule held a steady vehicle rotation of 11 RPM [R024].

In the LUCI simulated lunar-gravity burn, the acrylic (PMMA) rod flame tip spread at 0.15 cm/s [R007].
- For comparison, the 1 g ground burn gave 0.40 cm/s [R008].

These Saffire tests ran below 60 kPa:
- VI-2, SIBAL cloth: 54.1 kPa [R029]
- VI-3, two-sided PMMA: 54.6 kPa [R053]
- VI-4, one-sided PMMA: 55.2 kPa [R031]

- Feier et al.: thin cellulose (Kimwipes) burned upward on the NASA KC-135 aircraft at 0.1, 0.16 and 0.38 G [R098]
- Sacksteder et al.: Kimwipes thin cellulosic tissue burned upward and downward on the NASA KC-135 aircraft in partial gravity [R092] [R093]
- The FM2 poster also reports SIBAL fabric burns in lunar gravity via a lunar-gravity centrifuge and parabolic flight [R076]

No evidence: The rows have no cotton jersey spread rate in lunar gravity at 34% oxygen.
Nearest tests:
- Saffire V-2 cotton jersey in orbit at 70.7 kPa and 26.2 mol % oxygen: burn duration 200 s [R028]
- Saffire V-2 cotton jersey: steady-state flame size 10.0 cm [R066]
- Saffire V-2 cotton jersey: burned steadily for 300 s while the fan was on [R068]

No evidence: The rows contain no Nomex tests aboard the space station.
Nearest tests:
- BASS-II in the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox: 24 PMMA rods burned in concurrent (stagnation point) flow [R081]
- Saffire V-2 cotton jersey in orbit: burned steadily for 300 s while the fan was on [R068]
- LUCI SIBAL fabric and PMMA rod in simulated lunar gravity: the burn lasted over 2.5 min [R026]

No evidence: The rows give no heat release measurement from the LUCI flight.
Nearest tests:
- LUCI PMMA rod in simulated lunar gravity: peak instantaneous flame base spread rate 0.6 mm/s (approximate) [R022]
- LUCI PMMA rod in simulated lunar gravity: total flame base spread about 6 cm until extinction [R012]
- LUCI SIBAL fabric in simulated lunar gravity: chamber oxygen fell to about 18% during the burn [R016]
Refused: I will not estimate or guess a value that is not in the evidence rows.
